page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. The running head is at the top, with the page number beside it. No margin notes. The catchword "ut" stands alone at the lower right.

main_text.p: beret. quo suo instituto non Iurisconsultorũ dignitatem ac splendore imminuit: imò verò potius auxit, atque amplificauit: sed numerum duntaxat eorum qui consulentibus responderét circumscripsit, ut certis tantùm ac dele-ctis viris ea potestas tribueretur. qua de re Pomponius in L.2:De orig.iur. ita scribit: » Primus Divus Augustus, ut » maior iuris auctoritas habe-» retur, cŏstituit, ut eius auctoritate responderent. Et ex il-» lo tempore peti hoc pro beneficio coepit. Et ideo optimus princeps Adrianus, cùm » ab eo viri praetorij peterent, ut
main_text.notes: The running head is decorative and could not be read; the number before it appears to be "II.". Line-end hyphen in "auctoritate" (printed "auc to-" / "ritate") is unclear, so the word is written whole. "L.2" is uncertain. The "»" marks at the start of each line of the Pomponius quotation are printed and kept as they stand. Dark stains and marks at the left edge are not printed text and are left out. Long s is written as plain s throughout.
